questions.question: AQ5. Find the adjoint of [[1,2,-2],[-1,3,0],[0,-2,1]]. Verify that this matrix and its adjoint are inverses of each other. (T.U. 2052)
questions.solution: det = 1 (computed in Ex 9.3 Q9). adj = [[3,2,6],[1,1,2],[2,2,5]] (matches the printed key, p283). A(adj) = 1·I = I since det = 1, so they are inverses.

questions.knowledgeNote: Inverse exists iff det != 0; det = -5 here.
questions.question: AQ6. When does a matrix have its inverse? If A = [[1,2,-1],[2,0,1],[0,3,-1]], find its inverse. (HSEB 2052)
questions.solution: A (square) matrix has an inverse iff its determinant is non-zero. det A = 1(0-3)-2(-2-0)-1(6-0) = -3+4-6 = -5. Cofactor/adjoint computation gives adj A = [[-3,-1,-2],[2,-1,-3],[6,-3,-4]]... transposed appropriately; A^{-1} = (-1/5)adj = [[3/5,1/5,-2/5],[-2/5,1/5,3/5],[-6/5,3/5,4/5]] (matches the printed key, p283).
questions.source: Sukunda Basic Mathematics Grade XI, Ch.9 Additional Q6 (HSEB 2052); book p282 = PDF p309 (vision read)

questions.question: AQ10. State the conditions for adding/multiplying two matrices. If A = [[1,2,3],[4,5,6],[7,8,9]] and B = [[1,0,-1],[-1,0,1],[1,1,-1]], verify (AB)' = B'A'. (T.U. 2055S)
questions.solution: Addition: same order. Multiplication: columns of first = rows of second. AB computed entrywise (3x3); (AB)' vs B'A' agree entry by entry (both 3x3).
